title: Anthropic Workshop: Build Agents That Run for Hours — Ash Prabaker & Andrew Wilson
talk_summary: Anthropic engineers describe how long-running agent harnesses evolved from fresh-context Ralph loops to a planner/generator/adversarial-evaluator pattern where separate context windows and a negotiated 'contract' of testable criteria replace self-review. They emphasize that self-evaluation is a trap, that harnesses must be re-tuned as models change, and that reading raw traces is the primary debugging loop.

takeaways.technique: Adversarial evaluator with separate context, not self-review
takeaways.what_they_do: Split builder and critic into separate agents with separate context windows and system prompts; the critic drives the live app (Playwright) rather than reading diffs, and returns critique to the builder in a loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: self-evaluation, very much a trap. Just use an adversarial evaluator

takeaways.what_they_do: Before writing code, generator proposes feature + tests and evaluator pushes back on scope/weak tests/missing edge cases via files on disk until both agree; evaluator then grades against that contract, not the original spec.
takeaways.evidence_quote: before the generator actually goes ahead and writes a single line, we have the two agents basically negotiate what done actually means

takeaways.technique: Written rubrics for subjective quality, few-shot calibrated
takeaways.what_they_do: Encode taste as an explicit weighted rubric (design, originality, craft, functionality) calibrated with few-shot reference examples so the evaluator's judgment converges on theirs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can't grade taste, but, you know, we think you can if you have a a strong enough opinion on it and you just kind of write it down

takeaways.technique: Filesystem as shared state + breadcrumb logs
takeaways.what_they_do: Long-running loops persist state to files (feature list JSON, progress file, learnings JSON with tried/evaluated/fixed entries) instead of relying on context windows; JSON chosen because models overwrite markdown less.
takeaways.evidence_quote: big fan of just using a file system for shared state um instead of kind of leaning on context windows

takeaways.what_they_do: Planner one-shots a deliberately high-level sprint spec; granular technical planning is left to builder/evaluator because planner errors cascade across sprints.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's very likely to still make an error, but when it does make an error, it's going to cascade

takeaways.technique: Read raw traces to tune harness; agent-assisted trace grep
takeaways.what_they_do: Primary debugging loop is reading full agent transcripts by hand to find where judgment diverged, then tuning prompts; optionally pipe transcripts to another agent to flag issues as a first pass.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The primary debugging loop was this, and not necessarily running more experiments. It was reading what the agent actually did
